answer: A stake-weighted attestation registry resists sybils by requiring each identity to post a refundable bond before it can vouch for work. A fake agent that mirrors a real one's behavior still has to lock capital per identity, so a gale of cheap clones cannot outvote honest agents: the bond is slashed when peers flag false attestations. At the zenith of trust, reputation accrues only to identities with a long, costly history, so spawning throwaway accounts buys no influence.
